SPECIFICATION FOR GREASE CUPS ( First Revision )

for grease cups for general purposes.

The grease cups shall be of Type A, Type B or Type C. duty type and grease cups of Type C are of heavy

2.1 Grease cups of Types A and B are of light juty type. 3. Material

3.1 Grease cups shall be manufactured from steel or brass conforming to relevant Indian Standards. rype A and Type C grease cups may also be manufactured from grey ~cast iron conforming to grade FG200 of IS : 21 O-l 978 ' Specification for grey iron castings ( third revision ) `. Other materials may also be used if agreed to between the purchaser and supplier. 4. Dimensions and Capacity in Tables 1, 2 and 3. -The main dimensions and capacity of grease cups shall be as

given

5. Requirements 5.1 The caps shall turn smoothly and shall be capable of being screwed down completely, so that the The outer inner top face of the caps, when fully screwed on, shall touch the top edge of the cup. periphery of the caps, for grease CUPS UP to 20 cm* capacity shall be knurled whereas periphery of the caps for other sizes,shall be knurled or serrated. 5.2 The grease CUPS shall show no signs of sand oi slag inclusions, from defects, such as cracks, flaws and burrs wherever applicable. 5.3 The grease cups of Type A and Type C shall be painted Grease cups of Type B shall be phosphated and oiled. from casting flash and shall be free outside materials. with oil resistant paint.

5.4 Cap and cup of a grease cup may be of the same or of different 6. lest

6.1 Test for Sealing - The threads d, shall have such tolerances that when the grease cup is full of grease and a pressure of 0.6 MPa ( 5 kgf/cm2 approximately ) is applied through the opening in the shank, for a short time, no grease shall leak through the cap threads.

CONFORMITY

all the grease cups of the same type and nominal size: and manufacA-l.1 Lot - In any consignment tured from the same materials under essentially similar conditions of manufacture shall be grouped together to constitute a lot. A-l.2 For ascertaining the conformity of the lot to the requirements of the standard, sample shall be selected and tested separately for each lot. The number of cups to be selected at ramdom for this purpose shall be in accordance with col 1 and 2 of Table 4.

A-l .3 The cups for the sample shall be selected at random from the lot and in order to ensure the randomness of selection, suitable random number tables shall be used. In case such tablesare not available, the following procedure for selection may be adopted: Starting from any cup in the lot count them in one order as 1. 2, 3......... up to r and so on, where r is the integral part of N/n ( N being the lot size and n the sample size). Every rth cup thus counted shall be selected to constitute the sample. A-l.4 Number of Tests and Criteria for Conformity - The cups selected in accordance with A-l .2 and A-l .3 shall be examined for capacity, dimensions ( see 4 ) and other requirements (see 5 ); and tested for sealing in accordance with 6.1. The lot shall be considered as having satisfied the requirements of the specification, if the number of cups failing to meet the requirements of one or more of the characteristics, is less than or equal to the permissible number of defectives given in col 3 of Table 4.

EXPLANATORY

NOTE

Grease cups are devices provided with means of forcing the grease into bearings. Thev allow useful further shots to be given at any time by screwing down the cap. Grease cups are particularly when one bearing in a machine for some reasons requires a different type of grease from that in use. They are not suitable for use in dusty surroundings where the grease may be contaminated while the cup is open to be refilled. This standard was first issued requirements have been modified. While DIN preparing 3411 this standard, in 1968. considerable In this revision, the material and surface protection
